raw_case_text: A 58-year-old male had a history of end-stage renal failure with 3 kidney transplantations (1979, 1981 and 2008). He had previous chronic hepatitis B, legionellosis, chronic Q fever and cytomegalovirus infection. The last renal transplantation was associated with acute rejection requiring a combination of anti-thymoglobulin, plasma exchanges, rituximab, mycophenolate mofetil 1g/d, tacrolimus 4.5mg/d and prednisone 10 mg/d. In 2004 Leishmania PCR in blood was positive (Fig 1B). L-AmB treatment initially induced clinical cure. Relapse occurred in August 2009 when plasma exchanges and corticosteroids boluses were administered for the graft rejection. Fever, anemia (Hb = 9.1g/dL) and leukopenia (leukocytes = 1600/mm3) were observed, along with 431 Leishmania per ml of blood (assessed by quantitative PCR). L-AmB (induction total dose, 40 mg/Kg) provided improvement and reduced parasitemia to 6.9 Leishmania/ml. A second recurrence with fever and a rise in parasitemia to 29.6 Leishmania/ml occurred in January 2010 during monthly maintenance administration of 3 mg/kg of L-AmB. High-dose L-AmB was reintroduced followed by miltefosine for 4 months. Parasitemia decreased but remained positive (0.4 Leishmania/ml) and number of CD4 lymphocytes increased from 87 to 147/mm3. A third recurrence was reported in July 2010 with fever, 29.8 Leishmania/ml and positive Leishmania culture from venous blood. L-AmB was reintroduced, followed by maintenance infusions for 4 months, 3 mg/Kg every 3 weeks plus downgrading of immunosuppressive therapies. As symptoms persisted, infusions were performed once-weekly and then twice-weekly. Parasitemia decreased from 88 to 0.6 Leishmania/ml but a fourth recurrence occurred in April-June 2011 with fever, leukopenia (leukocytes = 1200/mm3, CD4 lymphocytes = 186/mm3), anemia (Hb = 9.1g/dL) and parasitemia at 40 Leishmania/ml. Patient refused to increase the L-AmB dose, it continued at 3 mg/Kg twice-weekly. Transplant nephrectomy was performed in November 2011 and chronic dialysis reinstituted. In February 2012, fever, splenomegaly, anemia (Hb = 8.6g/dL) and thrombocytopenia (platelet count = 50,000/mm3) were observed with 12,870 Leishmania/ml and 60,440 Leishmania/ml of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid. Thereafter, meglumine antimoniate adapted to renal clearance was administered daily for 28 days, then 1-3 times/week for maintenance. Liver function remained normal. ECG showed a T-wave inversion but troponin remained normal. Fever and sweats resolved, spleen size decreased from 21 to 17 cm, and blood counts normalized in 4 weeks, number of CD4 lymphocytes = 833/mm3 in June 2012,. Leishmania blood PCR and cultures became negative within a month and remained negative over eight monthly evaluations until death in January 2013 due to hypovolemic shock following a dental extraction.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 58-year-old male three-time kidney transplant recipient presented with four relapsing episodes of visceral leishmaniasis characterized by recurrent fevers, sweats, splenomegaly, and pancytopenia between 2009 and 2012.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Following a third kidney transplant in 2008 complicated by acute rejection (treated with ATG, plasmapheresis, rituximab, MMF 1 g/day, tacrolimus 4.5 mg/day, and prednisone 10 mg/day), the patient—who had previously been cured of visceral leishmaniasis in 2004 with liposomal amphotericin B (L-AmB)—experienced four successive relapses of visceral leishmaniasis (August 2009, January 2010, July 2010, and April-June 2011) despite high-dose and maintenance L-AmB, 4 months of miltefosine, immunosuppression reduction, and transplant nephrectomy with return to hemodialysis in November 2011. In February 2012, he presented with a severe fifth episode marked by fever, night sweats, massive splenomegaly, anemia, and thrombocytopenia.
subjective.past_medical_history: End-stage renal disease status post three kidney transplantations (1979, 1981, and 2008; transplant nephrectomy in November 2011 and return to chronic hemodialysis); acute graft rejection in 2008-2009; visceral leishmaniasis first diagnosed in 2004; prior history of chronic hepatitis B, legionellosis, chronic Q fever, and cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for recurrent fevers, night sweats, and left upper quadrant fullness/splenomegaly across relapses (2009-2012). Immunosuppressive medications (prior to Nov 2011 nephrectomy): mycophenolate mofetil, tacrolimus, and prednisone.

objective.physical_examination: Recurrent fevers and splenomegaly (measuring 21 cm in February 2012, decreasing to 17 cm after meglumine antimoniate therapy).
objective.routine_investigations: August 2009 relapse: Hb 9.1 g/dL, WBC 1,600/mm3. April-June 2011 relapse: WBC 1,200/mm3, Hb 9.1 g/dL. February 2012 relapse: Hb 8.6 g/dL, platelets 50,000/mm3. During February 2012 meglumine antimoniate treatment: liver function tests remained normal, and ECG showed T-wave inversion with normal serum troponin.
objective.advanced_workup: CD4+ T-lymphocyte counts were 87/mm3 (rising to 147/mm3 in 2010), 186/mm3 (April 2011), and 833/mm3 (June 2012). Quantitative blood Leishmania PCR documented serial relapses: 431 Leishmania/mL (Aug 2009, reduced to 6.9/mL after 40 mg/kg L-AmB), 29.6/mL (Jan 2010, reduced to 0.4/mL after L-AmB + miltefosine), 29.8/mL with positive venous blood Leishmania culture (July 2010), 40/mL (April-June 2011), and a peak in February 2012 of 12,870 Leishmania/mL in blood and 60,440 Leishmania/mL in bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) fluid.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Diagnosed with chronic, multi-relapsing visceral and pulmonary leishmaniasis refractory to liposomal amphotericin B (L-AmB) and miltefosine in a heavily immunosuppressed three-time renal transplant recipient with a remote history of CMV, HBV, Q fever, and Legionella infections (confirmed by serial quantitative blood Leishmania PCRs peaking at 12,870/mL, positive blood culture, and BAL Leishmania PCR of 60,440/mL). Following transplant nephrectomy (Nov 2011) and severe relapse in February 2012, treatment with renal-adjusted meglumine antimoniate (daily for 28 days followed by 1-3x/week maintenance) achieved complete clinical resolution, splenic regression (21 to 17 cm), normalization of blood counts, CD4 recovery to 833/mm3, and persistently negative Leishmania blood PCR and cultures for 8 months until the patient died in January 2013 from hypovolemic shock after a dental extraction.
